messages.author: fc22cb727156ff4f
messages.subject: using 'each' in plyr
parts:
Hi everyone,

I am trying to use the helper function 'each' and I am hitting some
errors, sometimes different while the situations look the same. Any
insight is appreciated:

library("plyr")
d = data.frame(x=rep(1:2,5), z=runif(10))
# > d
# x z
# 1 1 0.7816113
# 2 2 0.6803406
# 3 1 0.6873345
# 4 2 0.5104255
# 5 1 0.7226360
# 6 2 0.9734474
# 7 1 0.8704620
# 8 2 0.3806005
# 9 1 0.5689569
# 10 2 0.4572897

ddply(d, .(x), min)

ddply(d, .(x), max)
# this returns 1 and 2, showing that, for each level of x, the whole
data.frame is passed to max
ddply(d, .(x), colwise(max))
# Using 'colwise', max computes the column-wise maxima and therefore
is more akin to
ddply(d, .(x), mean)
# which, by default, operates column wise

# now with 'each':

ddply(d, .(x), each(max,min))
# ok

ddply(d, .(x), each(max,mean))
# Error in proto[[i]] <- fs[[i]](x, ...) :
# more elements supplied than there are to replace
# My guess is that the error is caused by the fact that one function
operates column wise while the other does not.

# But this also fails, with a different error message
ddply(d, .(x), each(colwise(max),mean))
# Error in .fun(.data[[i]], ...) : Not a data.frame!
# I guess that means that the split according to x does not produce a
data.frame in each element, although it should...
split(d, d$x)


d = data.frame(x=rep(1:2,5), y=rep(2:1,5), z=runif(10))

ddply(d, .(x,y), colwise(min))
ddply(d, .(x,y), colwise(max))
ddply(d, .(x,y), mean)
ddply(d, .(x,y), colwise(median))
# OK, all good

ddply(d, .(x,y), each(max,min))

ddply(d, .(x,y), each(colwise(max),colwise(min)))
ddply(d, .(x,y), each(mean,colwise(median)))
# Both output the same error
# Error in .fun(.data[[i]], ...) : Not a data.frame!
# Which I still don't understand

Thanks in advance for your help.

JiHO

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: using 'each' in plyr
parts:
Hi Jiho,

As a general tip when diagnosing problems with ddply, try using dlply
instead, so you can see what the individual elements being combined
are.

> ddply(d, .(x), each(max,mean))
> # Error in proto[[i]] <- fs[[i]](x, ...) :
> #  more elements supplied than there are to replace
> # My guess is that the error is caused by the fact that one function
> operates column wise while the other does not.

That's basically correct - each expects every function to return a
single value, and mean is returning a data frame.

>
> # But this also fails, with a different error message
> ddply(d, .(x), each(colwise(max),mean))
> # Error in .fun(.data[[i]], ...) : Not a data.frame!
> # I guess that means that the split according to x does not produce a
> data.frame in each element, although it should...

dlply(d, .(x), each(colwise(max),mean)) is informative
each is returning a list!

Unfortunately colwise and each are currently compatible - mainly
because colwise returns data frames and each works individual values.
The following should work, but fails silently :(

ddply(d, .(x), colwise(each(mean, max))


Hadley
